analysis_trace.findings: NCT04260698 is an expanded access program (EAP) of omidubicel-onlv for allogeneic transplantation in patients with hematological malignancies. It is a single-arm, non-comparative expanded access study, not a randomized controlled trial. The primary endpoint is time from transplant to neutrophil engraftment, assessed by day 42 post-transplant.

Hematological malignancies requiring allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). Omidubicel is an ex vivo expanded umbilical cord blood product (nicotinamide-expanded) used as an alternative donor graft source.

Patients with hematologic malignancies undergoing allo-HCT who lack a suitable matched donor and receive omidubicel as the graft source. Population is broadly similar to the pivotal Phase 3 trial (NCT02730299) and the EAP cohorts reported in the literature.

Omidubicel is a nicotinamide-based ex vivo expanded cord blood unit. Nicotinamide (NAM) inhibits differentiation and enhances homing/engraftment of CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, yielding higher CD34+ cell doses and faster neutrophil recovery versus unmanipulated cord blood.

Endpoint is time-to-event: time from transplant to neutrophil engraftment (ANC ≥500/µL for 3 consecutive days), censored at day 42. The contract labels endpoint_type as 'not_evaluable' but the measure is clearly a time-to-event endpoint. I forecast median time to engraftment and day-42 engraftment probability.

Omidubicel has an established safety profile from the pivotal Phase 3 trial and EAPs. Key risks include graft failure, infections during neutropenia, and GVHD. No new safety signal specific to this EAP was retrievable within cutoff.

Primary risk is delayed or failed engraftment. However, omidubicel consistently shows faster engraftment than unmanipulated cord blood. EAP populations may include higher-risk patients, slightly widening uncertainty.

Direct evidence: the EAP results abstract (MED/40204073, 2025-04-08) and pooled analysis of five prospective trials (MED/36775201, 2023-02-10) report omidubicel engraftment outcomes. Pivotal Phase 3 (NCT02730299) showed median neutrophil engraftment ~10-12 days vs ~20 days for cord blood, with ~96% engraftment by day 42. EAP abstracts report consistent rapid engraftment. These support a median time to engraftment of ~11-13 days and high day-42 engraftment probability (~95%).

Could not retrieve full-text numeric results (living-record fetch blocked; registry 403). Numeric anchors are from abstracts/titles and prior knowledge of the pivotal trial. Exact EAP median time-to-engraftment value not directly retrieved; forecast is extrapolated from pivotal trial and EAP abstract titles indicating successful engraftment.
